findings.description: When max_pages truncates the page list, total_chars still reports content.length (the full document length), not the sum of returned page text. Consumers using total_chars to verify completeness or to gauge received data may be misled. If the intent is to report total document size this is fine, but the semantics are ambiguous and could cause incorrect behavior in downstream logic.

max_pages is not validated. A negative value (e.g., -1) causes Array.prototype.slice(0, -1) to return all pages except the last, which is almost certainly unintended. A value of 0 returns an empty pages array while total_chars still reports the full length. Consider clamping to a minimum of 0 or 1.

independent_verifier.summary: No security vulnerabilities found. The function uses a simple string split (no regex, so no ReDoS risk), does not merge user input into objects (no prototype pollution), makes no network calls (no SSRF), and delegates filesystem access to the VFS layer (path traversal is the VFS's responsibility). No credentials are handled. Error propagation from vfs.readText is left to the caller, which is acceptable. Two low-severity correctness notes regarding max_pages validation and total_chars semantics when truncation occurs.
